articleTitle: Adaptive Evaluation for Barriers Elimination: The OpenEDR4C Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The demands of contemporary work and education environments, embodied in Industry and Education 4.0 paradigms, have caused special attention to reducing the digital and educational gap among marginalized students and lifelong learners. Adaptive learning has become a relevant strategy to increase student engagement as it fosters better inclusion, equity, and learning outcome results. Sustainable Development Goal No. 4, Quality of Education, will be reached when every resource, platform, and program can be accessed by individuals regardless of their background, abilities, or capacities in every moment of their lives. The OpenEDR4C is a digital platform created to offer open educational resources (OERs) to scale up the Complex Thinking mega-competence through social, scientific, and technological entrepreneurship training. The platform is also designed to eliminate barriers in five dimensions across the learning path offered by each student according to a self-declared profile. The framework sets a differentiated pathway for the learning experience built with a decision tree and diverse multichannel educational resources. The pilot implementation of the platform allowed the final development stage to validate the functional platform launch. The findings of this study are a helpful contribution to digital education environment design and conceptualization, as they offer (1) a tool for inclusive and accessible platform conceptualization, (2) a profiling strategy framework for adaptive learning paths, and (3) the identification of classes or groups of users based on their needs and characteristics to offer the corresponding content.

articleTitle: Proposal and Evaluation of STEAM Educational Materials Aimed at Creating a Related Population for University Students
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach to empower communities by cultivating scientifically literate digital talent through tailored STEAM education. Our goal is to deepen individuals' connections with their local environments, enhancing their ability to contribute to community problem-solving. We aim to elevate awareness of local challenges and solutions, especially through IoT and AI technologies. Preliminary findings from workshops with 72 participants indicate improved engagement and understanding of these issues, showing promise for this model in fostering community development and innovation. This initiative not only promotes scientific literacy but also encourages a proactive stance towards addressing community needs, suggesting potential for broader application and impact.

articleTitle: Project-Driven Flipped Classroom Develop Digital Competences in Preschool Education Students
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Digital competency is one of the most important competencies for normal university students in the digital age. It will have a direct impact on the next generation they teach. At present, there are still some problems in the teaching content and teaching model. This study implements a project-driven flipped classroom teaching model for students by redesigning and developing a modern educational technology curriculum. 144 students participated in the experiment. Self-assessment was conducted in accordance with the ICT Teaching Competency Standards for Pre-service Teachers. The results show that project-driven flipped classroom solves the problem of learners' motivation. It can effectively improve the problems such as students cannot learn continuously, learn fragmented knowledge, and are easy to forget. At the same time, this study also points out flipped classroom requires university students have a certain level of self-management and self-learning ability. It is suitable for learning practical and operable knowledge and skills.

articleTitle: ChatGPT in Creative Writing Courses in Chinese Universities: Application and Research
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This paper explores the application of ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence system based on a large language model, in creative writing courses in Chinese universities. With the increasing prevalence of creative writing courses, traditional teaching methods encounter numerous challenges, including the discon-nect between theory and practice, insufficient timely feedback on student work, and restricted creative thinking. To address these challenges, we introduced ChatGPT as a supplementary teaching tool in creative writing classrooms. Drawing upon constructivism theory, we underscore the significance of student participation, interaction, collaborative learning, and personalized learning in fostering creative writing skills. Following a one-week writing training session and the implementation of a case study centered on the Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu, we assessed ChatGPT's effectiveness in three dimensions: realtime feedback, creative inspiration, and collaborative learning. Survey results revealed high student satisfaction with this teaching approach, acknowl-edging ChatGPT's role in providing prompt feedback, fostering creativity, and facilitating collaborative learning. Our study suggests that ChatGPT technology can expand students' creative horizons and elevate their creative proficiency. In conclusion, the successful integration of ChatGPT as a teaching aid offers novel insights for creative writing instruction and serves as a valuable reference for educators and researchers in the field of education.

articleTitle: Voice-Driven Emotion Recognition: Integrating Speaker Diarization for Enhanced Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In today's digital age, where online communication has become indispensable, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic, ensuring effective communication is paramount. Traditional emotion recognition systems, predominantly reliant on facial expressions, face inherent challenges in online environments where participants often opt for camera-disabled interactions. Addressing this gap, our research introduces a novel emotion recognition approach rooted in voice data. By integrating speaker diarization models, we enable intricate emotion analysis from voice data and juxtapose these findings with subjective evaluations from participant questionnaires. Preliminary results suggest that voice-based emotion recognition can potentially revolutionize the quality of online communication, laying the groundwork for future adaptive feedback systems.

articleTitle: Human-AI Pair Programming System: A Case Study on Railway Congestion Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: We are developing a system called SynergyAI based on a novel concept of human-AI pair programming. This concept does not focus solely on advising human programmers by AI but also stimulates the programmer's creativity and AI optimization ability. In human-AI pair programming, the human first chooses the data and AI operators. Then, the AI optimizes the parameters based on the correlation of the data. The output from the data is the prediction result and prediction factors. As a case study, we programmed a system to forecast railway congestion. In the case study, there are many parameter stations and spots along the railway line. The human programmer decides these parameters, producing an optimized program with suitable parameters. Based on human congestion factor input, the AI optimizes the relation of data to achieve high forecasting accuracy. As a result, we can predict the congestion factor with more than 90 % accuracy and about 70% improvement in terms of the complexity of the data flow. This shows the effectiveness of the pair programming system.

articleTitle: The Application of Arts Integration Technology for Online Learning in Early Childhood Education
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study aims to explore the effectiveness of arts integration in online preschool education by gathering the professional opinions of 50 experts and scholars in early childhood education through a Fuzzy Delphi questionnaire. The research findings highlight the multiple positive effects of arts integration for early childhood online learning environments. Through multi-sensory experiences involving visual, auditory and interactive elements, arts integration provides engaging learning experiences in the context of online learning. The expert consensus value from the Fuzzy Delphi data analysis authenticates that arts integration contributes to improving children's concentration, child-teacher interaction and parental involvement, and significantly benefits children's self-directed learning in online learning. The results of this study highlight the impact of arts integration in early childhood online learning and provide strong support for the education sector. The study encourages more educational institutions and educators to incorporate artistic elements into their teaching practices, thereby enhancing children's learning experiences and effectiveness. An arts integration approach not only stimulates children's interest in interactive learning, but also encourages artistic creativity, bringing dynamic new perspectives to children's online learning.

articleTitle: An Action Research on Blended Learning Model Applied to the Course Teaching
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In the context of higher education, blended learning has been extensively applied in course teaching. This paper employed an action research design, aimed at addressing the practical challenge of how to effectively integrate blended learning into the course teaching to cater to diverse learning preferences, ensure access to a wide range of learning materials, and cultivate practical skills relevant to future roles as professional preschool teachers. This action research involved 62 college students as participants, and conducted two surveys and one focus group interview for data collection. Based on the students' feedback and the researchers' self-reflection, the blended teaching model was modified in order to maximize its benefits for the learners. The modified course teaching model is comprised of before-class stage, in-class stage and after-class stage. Teachers and students shoulder different responsibilities in teaching and learning on each stage, but keep close collaboration during the entire process. Technical support is the key to realization of effective blended learning of this course. Implications and recommendations for future research were also discussed based on the results of this action research.

articleTitle: Viewing Experience Support Environment Based on Knowledge Experience Design
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Knowledge Experience Design (KED) is a software design method that converts people's experiences into information and shares and utilizes that knowledge among individuals, groups, and organizations in order for groups and organizations to carry out high-quality activities. By applying this method to viewing museum experiences, creating an environment using software that supports recording and sharing viewing experiences is possible. This environment provides viewers with a more exploratory way of viewing exhibits and allows them to gain new perspectives from other viewing experiences. These things lead to improving the quality of each viewing experience. In this work, the viewing experience support environment (VeXSE) designed based on KED was prototyped, and the results of trial experiments were evaluated and studied. The evaluation and discussion confirmed that VeXSE based on the KED contributes to viewers' exploratory viewing and gaining new perspectives from other viewing experiences. These things show that the idea of Knowledge Experience effectively creates software that promotes people's creative activities and supports their growth. This paper introduces KED, explains VeXSE based on KED, and then evaluates and discusses it based on the results of trial experiments.

articleTitle: Can Online Collaborative Learning Foster Knowledge Sharing Among Students?
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study aims at using stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) model and extending Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to examine the impact of online collaborative learning (OCL) on students' learning in idea organization and generation among peers in the higher education context. The model was tested with quantitative approach using a partial least square-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results from 289 respondents showed that most of the hypotheses were significant, except the impact of perceived ease of use on collaboration with peers. Overall, this research highlights the need to enhance OCL so as to foster knowledge sharing through idea organization and generation among students and their peers.

articleTitle: Utilizing Verbal Response Modes to Analyze and Enhance Group Discussion Dynamics: A Case Study on Speech Behavior and Conversational Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Currently, group discussion formats are extensively utilized in diverse real-world settings. In this work-in-progress study, we delve into an approach rooted in the functional facet of utterances, classifying them into eight distinct Verbal Response Modes (VRMs): (Disclosure (D), Edification (E), Advertisement (A), Confirmation (C), Question (Q), Acknowledgement (K), and Reflection (R)). This unique categorization is pivotal in understanding conversational tendencies among students across two salient group discussion paradigms: free-form and sequential discussions. Leveraging VRM coding, we observed that participants' discourse in sequential discussions is inherently more logical. Through a concise case study, this paper sheds light on the potential reasons behind the efficacy of certain discussions and introduces VRM as a promising tool for discerning conversational models. Understanding speech behaviors and conversational tendencies can significantly enhance group discussions in educational and professional settings.

articleTitle: Effective Methods in Cybersecurity Education for Beginners
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The need for highly skilled human resource development to respond to cybersecurity threats is increasing. In Japan, human resource development projects in cyber security, in the form of training based on exercises, are becoming more and more prevalent. Previous studies have indicated that the effectiveness of practical problem-solving education is different from that of traditional classroom education. In this study, we examined whether practical, exercise-based education is effective for Japanese students. We found that exercise-based education can improve students' knowledge of cyber security. For students who have limited knowledge of cyber security, we found that a combination of classroom lectures and practical training would be most effective.

articleTitle: Designing an Educational Chatbot for Enhanced Learning in Programming Courses
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study introduces a specialized Telegram chatbot developed for programming courses, which aims to boost student engagement and comprehension. The chatbot encompasses three principal functionalities: 1) A Query Module, which permits students to review assignment grades and previous code submissions, thus promoting a deeper understanding and the rectification of past mistakes; 2) A Learning Module, providing on-demand access to course content and instructional videos, that is tailored to individual learning paces, thereby increasing the convenience of instruction; and 3) A Q&A Module, that efficiently orchestrates the handling of student inquiries, offering notifications to both educators and inquirers, fostering a conducive Q&A atmosphere. Additionally, the research incorporates backend data analysis and student surveys to evaluate the chatbot's effectiveness. Preliminary results indicate that the chatbot relieves instructional burdens and enhances student motivation.

articleTitle: Visualizing and Revealing the Difference of Learner's Thought Process and Question Solving Method
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The objective of this study is to clarify the difference of each learner's question solving method and thought process as well as confirm the possibility of their visualization. In this study, we conducted an experiment with 13 participants. They were asked to categorize figures that varied in color, pattern, shape, and size into two groups. During the experiment, Participants' eye movements were recorded and their manipulation of figures were logged. The results showed that the participants could be divided into two groups according to the different question solving methods. Differences were observed between the two groups regarding the fixation time. However, no significant differences were observed between the two groups regarding the manipulation logs of figures. These results may suggest the possibility of visualizing the different thought process, as well as question solving method for each learner.

articleTitle: Exploring the Psychological Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Green Walls on Students and Educators
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Traditional landscape construction research has provided crucial insights into visual preferences and stress recovery for individuals. However, in urban educational environments, we have identified a lack of in-depth research on how basic forms in landscape design impact perceptions of students and educators. The quality of the educational environment is directly related to the effectiveness of student learning and teaching activities. Therefore, research on whether green walls can enhance the campus atmosphere and potentially contribute to teaching benefits holds significant practical value. This study combines Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) with questionnaire surveys to explore different compositions of green walls, such as curved and linear forms, and their impact on the learning environment. This study not only deepens our understanding of improvements in urban educational environments but also provides practical design references for creating more inspiring and comfortable learning spaces. Through this research, we aim to offer empirical recommendations for future urban educational environment designs and encourage broader applications to further enhance educational quality and student well-being.

articleTitle: Macroeconomic Experimental Teaching Platform: Design and Implementation from an Educational Psychology Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Macroeconomics, with its inherently abstract, systematic, and complex knowledge system, often poses challenges for students in terms of high cognitive load, limited initiative, and low self-efficacy. To alleviate these psychological barriers and enhance the learning experience, we have designed and implemented a macroeconomic simulation experiment platform grounded in educational psychology. This platform, compatible with both PC and mobile devices through Html5 technology, effectively simulates macroeconomic systems, supporting diverse interactive experiments. It offers multiple feedback methods, including sandbox simulations, dynamic curves, and instructional text, alongside interactive features like real-time parameter adjustments, curve snapshots, and marker points. This innovative approach not only facilitates situated learning but also decomposes complex macroeconomic systems into manageable sub-topics, smoothing the learning curve. The platform comprises three modules: a macroeconomic system, an interactive experiment platform, and an experiment control, which together provide a comprehensive and flexible learning environment. Through this platform, we have designed the IS-LM case experiment, tailored to address students' psychological issues and fears, demonstrating its considerable value in enhancing macroeconomics education.

articleTitle: Detection Of Crop Diseases And Insect Pests Based On Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study is based on a convolutional neural network model built with deep learning technology, and compares the mainstream target detection algorithms ResNet v2, Mask R-CNN, and YOLOv7 on the same tomato pest and disease data set. Select the algorithm with the best accuracy, average accuracy, and F1 score based on the model evaluation indicators. Experimental results show that the average accuracy (mAP) of ResNet v2 is 92.82%, Mask R-CNN is 94.90%, YOLOv7 is 95.17%, and IP YOLOv7 tomato pest detection is 97.35%, surpassing ResNet v2, Mask R-CNN and other networks. This study provides certain reference and inspiration for the development of tomato pest and disease detection technology, promotes the protection of ecosystem balance, ensures safe crop production, improves the level of agricultural intelligence, and contributes to achieving sustainable agricultural development and ensuring food security.

articleTitle: Breaking Language Barriers: The Power of Machine Translation in Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This research explored the potential of machine translation (MT) in enhancing the accessibility and inclusivity of online learning platforms, with Coursera serving as a case study. The study compared the performance of courses translated by humans (HT) to those translated by machines (MT) with a toggle feature allowing access back to the original content. The key metrics used were course completion rates and star ratings. The findings reveal that MT courses with the toggle feature have a 2.3 % higher course completion rate than standalone HT versions. Furthermore, MT courses have a higher likelihood of receiving a 5-star rating (88<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) compared to HT courses (84<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). These results consider potential confounding factors such as course pair fixed effects, product line, and learner tenure. Future research could involve experiments that randomly assign learners to different course versions or explore the potential of human translation with the toggle functionality to the original content. The findings have significant implications for practitioners in education and future research, highlighting the potential of MT in enhancing accessibility and inclusivity in online higher education.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Interaction between Online and Offline Second Language Classes
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Classroom interaction is a pivotal aspect of Second Language Acquisition (SLA). The rise of online education, bolstered by advancement in information technology, has sparked renewed interest in this field. Although many studies have centered on online classroom interaction, there remains a lack of the literature on direct comparison between online and offline classroom utterances. Addressing this issue, our study first introduces an adapted version of the Flanders Interaction Analysis System (FIAS) named the FIAS for Online and Offline Comparative Purposes. This modified system provides equivalent categories tailored for assessing interactions between the two settings. After pilot tests and preliminary interviews, observations were made of two groups of 41 students during two class hours respectively in online and offline environments. Detailed transcripts of these observations were then analyzed. The results indicated that there were no universal interaction patterns across the two platforms, but three significant findings were reported. Firstly, teachers remain key in facilitating interaction in online classes and students' adaptability to the virtual setting affects their performance. Secondly, diversified modes of interaction in virtual settings can fire participation enthusiasm among quieter students, bridging the gap of different personalities and language proficiency levels. Lastly, interviews with teachers and selected participants highlight the influence of peer motivation, language proficiency, activity design etc. The study offers practical suggestions for blended design of second language classes with the aspiration that these insights will be applicable across a variety of disciplines.

articleTitle: Investigating Chinese Learners ‘ Use and Perceptions of ChatGPT in EAP
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: ChatGPT is an AI technology that has the power to reshape language teaching and learning. This study employs a mixed method to investigate Chinese learners' use and perceptions of ChatGPT in EAP. The data were collected via a questionnaire with 149 students and semi-structured interviews with 9 students from a joint program at a key Chinese university. This research reveals that students use ChatGPT as a personal learning assistant, especially in collating sources, academic vocabulary and academic writing. Generally, they hold positive attitudes toward it but a fair proportion remain unsure due to unfamiliarity. The overwhelming majority of students believe that ChatGPT is not a replacement due to the humanistic features of courses delivered by teachers, but it is a supplement to EAP courses in the future. This study adds empirical evidence from students' perspectives in Chinese context and helps educators better understand the implications of AI technologies in EAP. In light of these, educators could focus on providing systematic curricula, interactive teaching, and personalized assistance and feedback.

articleTitle: Electronic Parts Counting in Physics Laboratory Using Difference of Gaussians Edge Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Small electronic parts counting in the physics laboratory is a challenging task. These small objects such as resistors, capacitors, and inductors are used in physics laboratories and because of their numbers and small size, are hard to count in a short period of time. The precise inventory of these small electronics parts is therefore compromised. In this paper we present the development of a small electronics parts counting system. The system employs object edges detection using the difference of gaussian operator. This technique is suitable for those small electronic objects which have clear boundaries. By adjusting relevant parameters sigma and threshold to suit the size of the objects, the edge images are clearly detected thus enable correct counting of the objects which leads to correct inventory of electronics parts. An alternative technique using the canny edge detector operator is also used as a comparison technique. The experimental results are precise.

articleTitle: A Support Tool for Instructors to Better Understand How Students Work on Assignments in Small Classes
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: We propose a tool to help instructors check the validity of Java programming assignments in Eclipse. The tool obtains the status of assignments being worked on in the university computer room and on home computers. The tool compares the creation process of similar assignments submitted by students. The experiment results showed that 32% of the edits were made to the program code on the day of the laboratory session, and the remaining 68% of the edits were made in the university computer room around 6:00 p.m. on or after the laboratory session. We found that 0.8% of the submitted assignments were very similar to each other, and further analysis of the edit histories of these program codes revealed that we could infer a certain degree of reference relationship between the assignments based on the relationship between the time of editing and the number of times edited.

articleTitle: Implementation of Infection Environment for White-hat Worm and Malicious Botnet Using Mirai Source Code
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In this paper, we create an infection environment for white-hat worms and a malicious botnet using Mirai source code. The environment also allowed us to observe the infectious capacity of the white-hat worm, focusing on the secondary infectious capacity. Secondary infectious capacity is necessary for the white-hat worm to get rid of the malicious botnet. To achieve this, this paper makes the following changes to the Mirai source code. Leaving an infected port open, making the process run in the background, and changing the function's compile options. We also added the concept of lifespan to the Mirai source code. And by creating secondary infectious capacity and life span we have created white-hat worms and malicious worms from the Mirai source code. Observations of the created environment revealed the following infections: (1) the case of only malicious botnet; (2) the case of only white-hat worm; (3) the case of a malicious botnet and white-hat worms. The results show that we should ensure a certain amount of infection time for white-hat worms. Under the conditions of this experiment, it was found necessary to set a lifetime of 180 seconds or longer, and to set a minimum of 100 units as the number of units to be searched at one time.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting Expectations of Computerized Cognitive Training Programs: A Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Computerized cognitive training (CCT) programs are apps, games, etc. for the purpose of improving cognitive abilities. In the past decade, a body of research has emerged investigating users' expectations of CCT, and whether or not those expectations contribute to a placebo effect in cognitive training. While previous research has found evidence for positive expectations of CCT, there is still no consensus as to what these positive expectations are based on. In this pilot study, a questionnaire was developed to measure expectations of CCT, as well as three other constructs that may be related to CCT expectations: belief in science, growth mindset, and intellectual curiosity. Based on data collected from 59 participants using paid and unpaid online platforms, the questionnaire was found to be reliable. There were differences in expectations of CCT depending on the platform through which participants were recruited, country of residence, and level of education. Growth mindset was lower in participants residing in European countries, there was a positive correlation between growth mindset and expectations of CCT for participants with a college degree, and a positive correlation between intellectual curiosity and knowledge of CCT for participants not residing in Europe or North America. Results are discussed in terms of how they can inform a larger follow-up study in this area.

articleTitle: A Gamification System for Acquiring Appreciation Perspectives in Museum
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: We find it difficult to remember the artifacts we viewed after visiting the museum. In this paper, we propose a guidance system for museums that aims to make the ar-tifacts more memorable to visitors. This is achieved through the implementation of Mandala Bingo, a game inspired by bingo. The system targets the National Museum of Ethnology (a.k.a. Minpaku) and incorporates gamification into the Minpaku Guide. The objective is to enable users to appreciate the artifacts based on their unique perspectives, making the artifacts more memorable. The evaluation results indicated that visitors became more conscious of the connections between the features of the artifacts. However, one participant mentioned that he became too focused on searching for the artifacts to be used in Bingo. An important future task is to conduct long-term experiments to measure the retention of memories.

articleTitle: Design Knowledge Graph-Based Recommender System for Engineering Pedagogy
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: There is an increasing interest in engineering pedagogy to design a knowledge graph-based recommender system and apply it to help with programming skills teaching. The emergence of artificial intelligence brings the knowledge graph as a pivotal tool for research and learning in the information age. This study aims to explore the process of the recommender system design and apply it in engineering pedagogy spanning from conceptualizing students' abstract learning ideas to addressing their practical challenges. The subject of the study is postgraduate students from two different teaching styles universities. The case study is used as the main research method to collect both quantitative and qualitative data. TP ACK Framework is applied and followed as the theoretical framework in both the technical system designing process and the programming skills teaching process. The limitations of the study and how future work can make up the research gaps in the current stage are discussed. It explored a significant research area with the potential to drastically change the pedagogical methods in engineering pedagogy.

articleTitle: Contextualized and Personalized Math Word Problem Generation Using GPT and Authentic Contextual Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This paper introduced an interactive system for generating contextualized and personalized mathematic word problems (MWP) from authentic contexts using the Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT). Our proposed Automatic Question Generation (AQG) system comprises (1) the authentic contextual information acquisition through image recognition by TensorFlow and augmented reality (AR) measurement through AR Core, (2) a personalized mechanism based on instructional prompts to generate three difficulty levels for learner's different needs, and (3) MWP generation through GPT with authentic contextual information and personalized needs. A quasi-experiment was conducted by recruiting 51 fifth-grade students to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed AQG on their geometry learning performance. The results revealed that students who learned with the proposed AQG outperformed students who learned with a decontextualized way on geometry learning performances. Therefore, our proposed AQG is useful for promoting mathematic problem-solving activity in an authentic context.

articleTitle: DAT (Data Analytics Tool): A Data-Driven Decision-Making Tool for Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Data Analytics Tool (DAT) is an application that collects and analyzes data in order to improve business processes and aid in discovering hidden trends and patterns thereby uncovering insights to make future data-driven and intelligent decisions. This project is aligned with the business and data analytic courses content of the University and intended to be used by the faculty members and students enrolled in these courses. With the utilization of DAT, the users can uniformly use it in simulating business analytics with the given data set. DAT development was based on the principles of lean methodology. Various technologies incorporated in the application were: data mining, statistical measures, forecasting, and decision analysis methods. These tools were implemented using Visual Studio and coded using C# because of its flexibility. DAT was evaluated for its effectiveness and efficiency as a data analytic tool for faculty members and students using the ISO/IEC 20510 software quality assurance standard with the factors: functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, and reliability. The weighted mean results per criterion were computed, and interpreted using the Likert scale model and resulted in the acceptability rate of the respondents

articleTitle: Can Online Meeting Platforms be Better Utilized in Teaching Scenarios? - A Study on the Impact of Online Meeting Layout on Learners
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Increasingly, higher education institutions are adopting online conferencing platforms for teaching activities. However, it also impacts the learning process and outcomes. The layout of online platforms influences learners' attention and learning behaviors. This research employed eye-tracking experiments to compare the effects of online meeting interface layouts and different forms of interactive comment presentations on learning activities. The results indicate that under the podium-style layout, learners' attention to the slide area and the speaker increased. Comments presented in a pop-up format more effectively captured learners' attention, simultaneously enhancing focus on relevant areas and yielding more positive user experience feedback. The findings of this study contribute to the enhancement of interface and experience design in online learning platforms.

articleTitle: A Product Recommendation Method by Analyzing Sales Volume, Sales Period, and User Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In recent years, the large amount of product information available on e-commerce websites has made it difficult for users to refer to it when shopping and selecting products. In particular, the comments posted by customers on e-commerce websites usually reflect the users' impressions and feelings about using the products objectively and realistically. Therefore, in order to provide guidance to customers who need to buy the products, we propose a product recommendation method based on the three critical dimensions of the product: sales volume, sales period, and user satisfaction. To do this, we use the sentiment analysis of product reviews to calculate the satisfaction score of the product. Then, this satisfaction score is combined with the sales volume and sales period of the product to calculate the comprehensive ranking score to provide users with a product ranking for recommending products with high satisfaction scores, large sales volumes, and long sales periods. Finally, we evaluate and discuss the proposed method using actual e-commerce data.

articleTitle: Facial Recognition: Decoding Emotions in Online Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Following the rapid increase in online communication and remote collaboration after the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been a heightened need to understand and manage emotional dynamics in virtual interactions. This study constructed and validated an online real-time emotion recognition system. Utilizing FaceMesh for facial landmark detection, the Fer2013 dataset for training, and the Xception deep learning architecture for emotion classification, the system efficiently deciphers emotions from real-time videos. It was observed that participants in two different groups showed a preference for a free discussion format when engaged in two distinct discussion modes. This observation aligns with the results from participant surveys, confirming the accuracy of the system of emotion predictions. The construction and validation of this system lay the foundation for the subsequent development of active communication model.

articleTitle: Study for Division of General-Purpose Software that Helps with Customization
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: To increase the use of heterogeneous hardware, we have proposed the concept of environment-adaptive software that automatically converts and operates program code once written so that it can be used appropriately in the environment in which it is placed. This paper proposes a new element of environment-adaptive software, a method that analyzes the code of general-purpose programs and allows users to add and change the processing they want to perform. The proposed method divides the application based on related processes and localizes changes based on the division boundaries, making it easier to add and change services. We check the sample applications can be automatically divided using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Game-Based Learning as an Effective Instructional Strategy for Improving Students' Critical Thinking and Collaborative Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: With the advent of COVID-19, almost all classroom teaching in higher education in Malaysia, were drastically converted to online. To enable more practical online learning to take place, blended learning approaches were adapted to address this necessity. However, over time, it was shown that students, when going online to learn content, experienced less interactions, and felt socially isolated. Literature has also shown that classrooms learning today still lack deep collaboration, and this was more prevalent during the COVID-19 education paradigm shift to the new normal of hybrid learning. Game-based learning has been posited to address this issues by providing more motivation and engagement to students. However, there is still a debate as to how effective is game-based learning in online education, as some studies have shown success, while some have shown little to none. Clearly these disparities poses a challenge to educators using game-based learning, and demands deeper investigation. This research seeks to look into the impact of game-based learning, embedded within a socio-constructivist environment, on students' critical thinking and collaborative learning. Findings from the study show that the game-based learning environment was very positively received by students, and was successful in impacting 3 areas: 1) learner engagement, 2) learner experiences and 3) technology support. Specifically, students reported positive experiences in the enjoyment, understanding, teamwork and real-world relevance constructs. A game-based learning (GBL) framework is proposed as a practical guide for educators seeking to adapt their classes to today's learner needs and cultivate improved students' critical thinking and collaboration skills in hybrid learning environments.

articleTitle: Recognition of Student Engagement and Affective States Using ConvNeXtlarge and Ensemble GRU in E-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The advent of online learning has revolutionized the educational landscape, significantly enhancing global access to and affordability of education. However, a critical challenge in this domain is the efficacy of online classes, particularly in the context of the feedback loop between instructors and students. A pivotal aspect of this challenge is the assessment of student engagement and other affective states in online learning environments, a task that is inherently complex due to its nuanced nature. In this paper, we introduce a novel spatio-temporal hybrid deep learning model that combines the strengths of ConvNeXtLarge with an ensemble of gated recurrent unit (GRU and Bi-GRU) models to detect and classify affective states of students from video data. This model adeptly handles the multi-label, multi-class nature of the problem, employing four parallel fully connected (Dense) layers for effective classification. Our model's performance is evaluated using the DAiSEE dataset, a publicly available resource that captures a range of student affective states in an online learning environment. The proposed model demonstrates promising results in identifying four key affective states of boredom, engagement, confusion, and frustration, with accuracy rates of 54.89%, 56.46%, 70.18%, and 79.32% respectively. These findings underscore the efficacy of our model in accurately gauging student affective states, thereby offering significant insights into the potential of spatio-temporal hybrid networks in this realm. The study demonstrates the feasibility of employing such models to enhance the quality of online education.

articleTitle: Enhancing Learning Effectiveness Through YouTube Kids: A Case Study of Arts and Craft Learning in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The YouTube Kids platform serves as an educational tool designed for children under the age of 12, allowing parents to exercise control over the educational content accessed by their children. Through YouTube Kids, children can engage in creative arts and crafts activities, enjoying both the process and achieving more effective learning outcomes. This paper aims to focus on 5 children, aged between 5 and 8 years. The study will employ observational data collection methods and open-ended interviews to gather valuable insights. This research explores the intricate relationship between various aspects of art and craft videos, encompassing content type, video duration, and audio-visual elements, and their impact on children's learning outcomes. Learning through video content entails a multimodal approach, engaging the visual, auditory, and kinaesthetic senses simultaneously. This method is expected to yield substantial learning benefits. The findings of this research are anticipated to provide valuable recommendations for video creators, particularly educators, to enhance the quality of arts and crafts education for children on YouTube Kids. Simultaneously, the insights derived from this study will contribute to improving the overall effectiveness of art and craft learning for children on the YouTube Kids platform.

articleTitle: Improving Water Knowledge Outcomes in Civil Engineering by Applying BIM
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Due to the developments in the field of digital technologies in construction, e-learning has become an essential part of civil engineering courses. Recent advancements in this field such as Building Information Modeling (BIM) have led to a renewed interest in its application to several courses in civil engineering. BIM is a widely used digital technology in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry. It can be used as a powerful learning tool to improve the outcomes of students in water courses. The study was implemented in a project-based learning (PBL) class under the framework of the new educational model Tec21 at Tecnologico de Monterrey University in Puebla campus, Mexico. At the end of the course a 5-question survey using Linkert scale was evaluated to investigate the usefulness of BIM digital technology across project groups. The results showed that BIM helped to better understanding project phases, and to visualizing the size of the elements in a digital real work environment.

articleTitle: A Study on Primary School Students' English Learning Motivation Through International Robot Competitions
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study explores the impact of integrating Dash robot competition topics into the fourth-grade information education curriculum. Teachers adopt the EMI (English as a Medium of Instruction) teaching approach to enhance students' motivation in both English learning and programming skills. Throughout the course, students actively participate in collaborative learning through group activities. The research methodology involves conducting a survey using “The Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire” to understand changes in students' motivation for learning the English language. Results from the motivation questionnaire clearly highlight the most significant improvement in the Value Component, indicating a noticeable enhancement in students' perceived importance and value of this learning experience. Changes in the Expectancy Component are also evident, reflecting heightened expectations for the course. From this, it can be inferred that the integration of educational technology into the classroom effectively stimulates and enhances students' motivation for learning. The anticipated outcomes of this study will contribute to introducing diverse learning styles into primary school students' language education.

Author Keywords: English as a medium of instruction

articleTitle: Integrating Side Information into Collaborative Filtering Recommendation Method in Online Course Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: To acquire non-formal education, one can access an online course platform. There are plenty of courses on those platforms, so the recommender system came up to help the user choose the one that matches their preferences. A recommender system with a collaborative filtering type is more suitable for non-formal education. Furthermore, a user might have some considerations for choosing a course. Therefore, we integrate side information into two collaborative filtering recommendation methods: Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR) and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). The side information incorporated into BPR via feature augmentation, while we use the HybridSVD scheme for the SVD. We also tried to scale the rating matrix to promote the unpopular classes. The results show that the best top-N performance was achieved using the scaled HybridSVD with the course concept similarity matrix.

articleTitle: Feature Mining Algorithm for Student Academic Prediction Based on Interpretable Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Predicting student academic performance is one of the pivotal issues of concern in the educational domain. With their outstanding predictive capabilities, neural network algorithms are widely used for predicting student academic performance. This paper primarily focuses on the crucial issue of the interpretability of deep neural network models in the field of educational data mining and proposes an interpretable deep learning model, namely Log-LassoNet, which is applied to educational data. This paper conducts modelling analysis on the China Education Survey data set by introducing noise as additional fake features. The model demonstrates satisfactory predictive and feature selection capabilities, outperforming current mainstream algorithms such as Lasso regression and random forests. Moreover, through feature mining, it was found that the expected and health-related features play an important role in forming high-level features that impact student academic performance, which provides a foundation for exploring the factors affecting students' academic performance.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Enhancing the Motivation of Young Learners in Intangible Cultural Heritage Education: A Creative Real-Time Finger Tracking System for Chinese Shadow Puppetry
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Many obstacles are causing Chinese shadow puppeteering, an endangered art form, to disappear. This state of affairs has been exacerbated by a number of factors, including the impact of varied entertainment options, aging puppeteers, declining audiences, and a dearth of youthful successors. This study suggests using real-time finger-tracking technology to manage shadow puppet performances in an effort to conserve and revive Chinese shadow puppetry. Eight young adults participated in a workshop and a comparison experiment as part of the research technique. They used joysticks to control actual shadow puppets at first, and then they used a wireless data-tracking glove to control virtual shadow puppets. The results show that young beginners find it difficult to operate a shadow puppet with just one hand. However, the learning curve for shadow puppeteering is much reduced with the advent of the real-time finger-tracking device. It also does a good job of encouraging the younger generation to interact with virtual puppets. The cutting-edge, captivating, and interactive technological components of the system appeal to the generation that was raised on digital devices and encourage their interest in and participation in virtual puppeteering. This work advances design, technology, and Chinese culture by offering a technical framework for upcoming research projects that utilize digital shadow puppetry archives in various contexts, such as the conception and production of animated films. This study aims to preserve and advance the rich traditions of puppetry by bridging the gap between traditional puppetry and contemporary digital encounters.

articleTitle: Support System for Learning the Issues Involved in Achieving Exit Strategies for University Venture Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of using the university venture database to identify the challenges faced by firms seeking to expand their sales size and number of employees by displaying an overall radar chart of the exit strategy factors of the firm. 14 companies were able to determine whether they had achieved an expansion in sales scale or number of employees, and the proposed methodology was applied to these companies. The results showed that the companies that were aiming to expand the scale of sales and the number of employees were conducting solid management practices to establish a business foundation, such as acquiring patents. This helps entrepreneurs and others not only to start their own businesses but also to maintain long-term management after starting.

articleTitle: A Visualization Analysis of Using Moodle Within English Language Teaching and Learning via CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Moodle, which stands for Modular Object-Oriented Dynamic Learning Environment, has been used to facilitate teaching and learning for more than twenty years. This study investigated the research on the application of Moodle for the purpose of teaching and learning English on a global scale. In general, the number of papers published each year increased significantly over the past fifteen years, despite a few fluctuations. Ukraine emerged as the most productive country and the Technical University of Košice contributed the largest number of papers. European and Asian scholars have played the most essential roles in the research. Yea-Ru Tsai, Arif Bakla, and Marta Gluchmanova stood out as the most prolific writers. However, complex collaborative networks of authors or institutes were not common, indicating the necessity to strengthen cooperation between authors and between organizations. Research in this area can be divided into three main themes: integrating digital technologies into Moodle-supported English teaching and learning, teachers' activities and professional development, and students' learning process. How the use of Moodle in English language teaching affects students' language learning and cognitive development has always been the most important research hotspot. Furthermore, it suggests that future research focus on the interdisciplinary study between this field and cognitive science so that students' cognitive development and language-skills development in the Moodle-supported English language teaching and learning could be further explored. Researchers could also study how to synchronize the use of Moodle and other educational technologies to better facilitate the teaching and learning of English.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation Experiment of a Classroom Support System for Programming Education Using Tangibles Educational Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In recent years, the utilization of tangible educational materials has attracted attention on educational settings. Because they provide hands-on learning experiences for beginners. This trend is also notable in the field of programming education. Such educational materials are employed in educational institutions worldwide. They liberate programming languages from small computer screen. On the other hand, classroom time is limited. When instructing more than 30 learners, it is hard for the instructor to provide adequate guidance for everyone. Consequently, they have to work extended hours, e.g., after-school hours. To address this problem, we have developed a classroom support system for programming education that complements the use of tangible educational materials. With this system, instructors can monitor the real-time progress of each learner during the class and analyze which parts of the program many learners find challenging. Based on these analytical results, instructors can provide appropriate instructions for individual learners and effectively conduct the class.

articleTitle: High School Students' Perception of AI and Its Future Impact on Education
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Different artificial intelligence (AI) based technologies and systems are gaining in a variety of uses, including personal assistants, chatbots, different suggestion engines, smart appliances etc. Usage of this technology is accompanied by various positive views, but also by a fair share of skepticism. Since ChatGPT has been introduced, there have been rising debates regarding AI and its effects on education, employment, ethics, security, and other areas. One of the important questions is how young people view this new technology and all its implications. The purpose of this study was to learn more about how high school students view and feel about AI. Research regarding AI was conducted among 124 high school students in classes I through IV (aged 15 to 19). Although new technologies are something they embrace, students also find that no AI technology can completely replace human beings in education. Despite having different viewpoints on the matter, they are optimistic about new technologies and think that AI tools would be beneficial for future teaching and learning.

articleTitle: The Role of Teacher Feedback in Shaping Student Achievement during U-Physics Exploration Activity Design
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the importance of teacher feedback in facilitating students' learning of physics using an educational app called U-Physics inside and outside the classroom. Furthermore, the study also explores students' perception toward the U- Physics exploration activity design. A total of thirty-six students was divided two groups namely, experimental group (EG) and control group (CG). Both used the same U-Physics app and the only difference between the groups lies in the provision of teacher online feedback. The finding shows that EG outperformed CG in terms of learning achievement. Teacher feedback within an online discourse significantly influences students' involvement in learning activities. It increased the participation of EG students through asking and answering questions, active posting, and task completion. As a result, it contributes to the enhancement of their cognitive development. Additionally, students perceived positively toward the U-Physics exploration activity design.

articleTitle: Fostering Self-Regulated Learning in a Flipped Classroom Approach and Developing Effective Web-Based Instruction for Pre-service Teachers of Mechatronics Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Despite the growing emphasis on self-regulation in diverse learning settings, its impact on web-based instruction development remains understudied. This research fills that gap by exploring how web-based training can foster self-regulation skills and improve student engagement. Mixed methods research was used to collect data from 24 pre-service teachers of Mechatronics Engineering majors. A paired sample t-test revealed a significant difference between learning engagement on pre-test and post-test after using the web-based training. The post-test mean scores increase, was significant (p < 0.05). The study also found that the majority of students had a high satisfaction with the teaching and learning process, its usability and capacity to make learning with themselves via web-based training (before class) and increase engagement in group discussion in class. These support students in concentrating during class.

articleTitle: EduCredPH: Towards a Permissioned Blockchain Network for Educational Credentials Verification System
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Education is an important component of society and most times, the main evidence of undergoing learning a topic or acquiring a degree is through a paper-based certificate, sometimes called educational or academic credentials. With the challenges faced by the Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) relating to security, privacy, and authenticity of their records, utilizing the upcoming technology to digitalize records is a good solution. Specifically, blockchain can provide a decentralized network with tamper-proof and non-repudiation characteristics. In this paper, Hyperledger Fabric was used to create a permissioned network that served as the backend for an educational credential verification system to assist the HEIs and third-party verifiers, and students/alumni to view educational credentials. The system architecture and implementation discussed may be used to implement an innovative approach to managing academic credentials. The performance of the chaincode deployed in the blockchain network was evaluated by having its endpoints tested as Application Programming Interfaces (API) for this system using Insomnia. The result of the evaluation showed that retrieving a credential runs with the average of 181.5 milliseconds (ms) while carrying 628 bytes of data. Overall, this paper has shown that a centralized system can be connected to a blockchain network while developing a new system to facilitate a smooth exchange of information.

articleTitle: A Proposal of Sentiment Analysis Approach for Comments Based on Semi-supervised Learning and Topic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study proposed an approach that can indi-vidually determine the corresponding sentiments for each topic mentioned in the comments. As a case study, we collected comments from 2 battle-royale games from the Steam platform. Using the results from this study to provide advice for game developers on areas where their games need further improvement and update, or develop new games via mining information from user comments of already released same genre games. We first fine-tuned the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model for classifying comments that are not related to games or do not contain enough content for thematic analysis. Second, utilizes Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) to extract topics from comments. At last, employ another BERT model to analyze user sentiment toward every topic in every comment. The experimental results can be obtained by comparing topics of different games which were scored by sentiment analysis. The highest score in the game NARAKA is the “Optimization” topic with 0.4964. In the game Z1, the “muti-gameplay” topic is 0.4393.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Automatic Questioning System Based on Question Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: As an important branch of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP) plays an important role in the field of education. Question-driven teaching is a necessary means of all kinds of teaching, and students' learning effect can also be tested through questions. In this paper, according to the demand of a large number of questions in the teaching scene, Question Generation (QG) algorithm in NLP is studied. A QG method based on pretrained language model is proposed. Based on this algorithm, an automatic questioning system is constructed, which can assist teachers to construct question banks and students to carry out reading comprehension. This research mainly introduces the construction and training of the pretraining QG model, the construction of Chinese question generation (CQG) dataset, and the construction of the automatic questioning system for teachers and students.

articleTitle: Research on the Reforming of Construction Safety Course Based on SPOC + MOOC
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: There are some problems in the traditional teaching model, such as outdated teaching concepts and lack of advanced thinking, innovation, and challenge. In order to solve these problem, the teaching team has conducted effective blended teaching pattern based on SPOC in the core course Construction Engineering Safety Technology and Management (hereinafter referred to as construction safety) in the Safety Engineering major. Through careful course design, the teaching content is scientifically divided and effectively connected in online and offline teaching. This includes pre-class online guidance, classroom discussion-based teaching, timely guidance and quizzes after class, and other multidimensional reinforcement to motivate and guide students' active learning. This fully mobilizes students' enthusiasm and autonomy in learning, creates a good learning atmosphere, and effectively improves students' learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Expectations and Possibilities of Using IoT in Education
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The use of information and communication technologies (ICT) in contemporary educational settings is remarkable. Researchers and teachers are actively exploring various methodologies to maximize the potential of ICT, emphasizing the need to enhance ICT skills for dynamic learning experiences. In Japan, education on the use of ICT is mandatory in university teacher training programs. However, ICT use in early childhood education and care is still limited. In other words, although ICT use is a mandatory part of the curriculum to be a kindergarten / nursery school teacher, its use in early childhood education is almost nonexistent. There are various arguments for and against the necessity of ICT in early childhood education. Countries such as the United States, Norway, and South Korea offer successful models. On the other hand, there has been little movement in Japan to utilize ICT in childcare, which the authors believe is an issue that needs to be addressed. Based on the authors' extensive research, this paper focuses on the introduction of ICT in childcare and proposes the educational use of the Internet of Things (IoT) as a solution. We delve into this topic and report on the transformative potential of the integration of ICT and IoT to shape the future of early childhood education.

articleTitle: Practical Report of Studying Unknown Programming Languages through Pictogram Contents Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: We have developed and proposed a web application called “Pictogramming,” designed to facilitate the learning of fundamental programming concepts through the creation of pictogram content. Pictogramming provides the opportunity to study general-purpose programming languages Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and block-based programming. We focused on research indicating the benefits of studying multiple programming languages, and thought that it is highly significant to design a curriculum for studying multiple programming languages through a unified concept, creation of pictogram contents by utilizing Pictogramming. In this curriculum, university students sequentially studied Python, JavaScript, block-based programming, and Ruby basics through Pictogramming. In the Ruby lesson of the curriculum, which was the final segment, students worked on same tasks as previous languages and answered questionnaires. The results showed that even with relatively simple lessons, students were able to grasp the fundamental concepts of multiple programming languages. Therefore, we have concluded that studying multiple programming languages through a unified concept is an efficient and effective approach.

articleTitle: Navigating Learning Pathways: A Multifaceted Approach to Understanding Student Engagement and Progress in Online Programming Courses
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In an era when online education is becoming increasingly prevalent, and many institutions are transitioning onto online platforms, it has become crucial to understand online learning behaviors. The user data kept by online learning platforms has supported relevant research that has made great strides in analyzing both engagement and dropout rates in online courses. In online programming courses, learners struggle to understand the code and even code by themselves, while instructors barely have access to check everyone's code and give advice in real-time. It becomes critical for instructors to quickly grasp how learners are progressing and encountering difficulties in their online programming learning. This study combines learners' programming activity data, click stream data from video learning, and textual data such as accompanying notes and questions. A visual representation that combines multiple learning data is proposed, and learners' Learning Trajectories Map in an online programming course is created from experimentally collected data. The results show a strong correlation between learners' programming activities and their engagement with the learning material. In addition, by comparing the learners' learning trajectories, it was possible to observe their different learning strategies, which provided more detailed clues for studying behavioral patterns and learner characteristics in online learning. This study introduces a new tool for educational evaluation, provides a more comprehensive perspective, and addresses the limitations of relying only on a single indicator for evaluation. It is of great significance to educational technology and computer-assisted education.

articleTitle: Design-Implementation Discrepancy Analysis for Mobile Application Interfaces Using Object Detection Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: With the rising number of mobile users, the demand for seamless application experiences intensifies, underscoring the importance of Graphical User Interface (GUI) design. Engineers strive to create user-friendly interfaces during the design phase, meticulously planning component layouts. In the implementation phase, translating this design into a functional interface is critical. The manual comparison of the implemented interface with the design, especially during manpower shortages, adds significant workload. To address this, we propose an automated comparison process. Design and implementation images are inputted, employing advanced image processing to identify objects. A similarity formula quantifies the resemblance, and the Hungarian algorithm efficiently matches components. Results are displayed visually, streamlining verification and enhancing mobile application development efficiency. Moreover, this automated process has educational significance in software engineering. It serves as a pedagogical tool, aiding students in understanding the alignment between system design and implementation, fostering a comprehensive grasp of the software development lifecycle.

articleTitle: Web Page Editor with Automatic Interconversion Function
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Web page editors have been proposed that allow for automatic refresh and display of web pages, as well as manual conversion from visual blocks to HTML text and vice versa. The web page editors are usually implemented as web applications, and it applies to this study as well. However, no software seems to have automatic interconversion function between visual blocks and HTML text. This study aims to create a web page editor capable of automatic interconversion between visual blocks and HTML text. The proposed web page editor can read local image files, which is usually impossible to automate in a web application, due to security constraints. We circumvent this difficulty by utilizing Chrome Extensions and the File System Access API. As a result, the user is once asked explicit permission for the access to a particular directory, and the access is granted thereafter for automatic interconversion. The web page editor was experimented in a Japanese school to evaluate its effectiveness, where most students responded affirmatively to a questionnaire about using it for learning.

articleTitle: Experiential Learning Spaces Through an Academic Software Application to Simulate Production Lines of Rigid Bodies
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Currently, there are various software applications to simulate production lines; however, some of them are expensive and require robust computing equipment. On the other hand, universities constantly try to generate courses that attract attention and motivate students. To achieve the above, it is proposed to use application software to simulate production lines in a course called Cyberphysical Systems II for university students of the Mechatronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, and Systems Engineering and Computer Technologies Engineering courses of the seventh semester. Through the application software used, an experiential learning space is created, in addition to having academic versions that are free for students. Different exercises were generated to evaluate the impact of using the software application, which was assessed using a checklist. At the end of the course, students were given a survey to find out their perception about the use of application software in their course. Their comments were also collected voluntarily to obtain their general opinion of the course. The results show that most students improved their grades as they solved the exercises, even though their difficulty level increased. The comments obtained were positive, as was their general perception of the course when using the production line simulation software.

articleTitle: Vocabulary Profiling of Reading Materials for Learning Chinese
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Since extensive reading is important for language learning, students should engage in extra-curricular reading as much as possible. To facilitate efficient learning, language teachers need to select reading materials at the appropriate difficulty level, and adapt them if necessary. This paper describes a text analysis and revision tool that assists teachers in preparing reading materials in Chinese. On the basis of a graded vocabulary list, the tool estimates the percentage of words in a text that are known to students at the target school grade. Further, it highlights words that are expected to be new vocabulary, and suggests alternatives that better fit the expected vocabulary proficiency at the target grade. Evaluation results show that the use of Forward Maximal Matching improves word matching with the vocabulary list, and that dynamic editing of word segmentation leads to more accurate assessment of the text difficulty level.

articleTitle: Gender-Inclusive Materials to Learn Programming through Data Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study introduces learning materials for introductory computer programming from the viewpoint of gender-inclusion. Despite gender-equal opportunities to learn information technology, girls and female students recognize computer programming as “boys' stuff.” One of the possible reasons is that programming education often incorporates male-dominated fields, such as mathematics and engineering. We have considered the approach of gender-inclusive programming education, and we have focused on data visualization to induce motivation in students who study programming in various majors. Finding interesting data and expressing it in an informative way using programming can enhance learners' motivation. This paper reports on the learning materials, including the original library and class practices.

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning in Programming Education with the Programmed Visual Contents Comparison Method
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
