abstract: This paper discusses the effectiveness of the Programmed Visual Contents Comparison Method (PVCC) for collaborative learning in computer programming education. Building upon our previous study, we proposed PVCC to assess panoramic understanding of programming and developed a testing system based on this method. Our results confirmed the PVCC method's ability to identify programming abilities related to panoramic understanding of programming. To evaluate the effectiveness of PVCC for collaborative learning, we conducted an experiment with a group of students at a graduate school. The inclusion of students contributed to a creative learning environment, where new ideas emerged during problem-solving activities. Our findings demonstrate that collaborative learning using the PVCC method is beneficial for students in the process of learning programming.

articleTitle: User Experience on a Culture-Based Learning Management System: Students' Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: User Experience (UX) refers to the individual experience of users when using software. An institution must analyze the user experience, especially for custom-built software. The goal of this study is to assess the UX to verify that e-Guro, the City College of Calamba's culture-based Learning Management System, satisfies student expectations. To achieve this purpose, an adapted culture-based questionnaire was used to assess UX. With an aggregate mean of 3.62, which was evaluated as acceptable, e-Guro satisfied the users' expectations in terms of goal content, usability objectives, accessibility goals, and engagement goals. The findings provide important insight into how to develop a culture-based learning management system to help achieve teaching and learning objectives more effectively.

articleTitle: A Design and Implementation of Stationery Product Recognition Method Using Two-Stage YOLO v8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: A company typically maintains a lot of stationery products, such as ball-pens, glue-sticks, and erasers, for daily use in the operations. However, their accurate managements will cost a lot or often be impossible. Currently, YOLO is a very popular model for object recognition using images due to high capabilities. In this paper, we present a design and implementation of a stationery product recognition method using the latest YOLO v8 model at two stages. The first-stage model recognizes the category of the target object from the given image. The second-stage model selects the specific product in the category. For evaluations, we prepare 795 images of 45 stationery products in 9 categories and train the two-stage YOLO models using NVIDIA's RTX-3060 GPU. Then, we measure the training time and the recognition accuracy of the proposal. The results show the effectiveness of the proposal.

articleTitle: A Transposed Hand Silhouette Interaction System Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: With the advance in new technology, the use of Virtual Reality (VR) or Augmented Reality (AR) techniques are successfully applied in the consumer market. Exhibition by hand silhouette is always an attractive application in many fields. A realistic exhibition in hand silhouette display is the most concern. However, it largely depends on the person's skill on hand exhibition and thus decreases the quality on the silhouette-based result. In this paper, we develop a transposed hand silhouette interaction system. To make a precise exhibition, we substitute the individual hand silhouette with a pre-defined hand silhouette template. It induces the important kernel for hand segmentation and classification which is used by the deep neural network. We build the whole system to make a precise and accurate hand silhouette exhibition in a transposed way. As a result, this innovative form of exhibition combined with technology is providing users with a fully interactive experience.

articleTitle: Structural Equation Modeling of Perceived Ability in Media and Digital Literacy among Japanese High School Students
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This research constructed and examined a structural model of Japanese high school students' perceptions of their own abilities in media and information literacy and digital competency to obtain instructional hypotheses for designing practical lessons which nurture these abilities from a lifelong learning perspective. A survey of 710 first-year Japanese high school students was conducted on the perceptions of abilities and learning motivations towards Media and Information Literacy (hereafter, MIL) and DigComp. The survey used a self-assessment scale developed in prior research, conforming to the frameworks of UNESCO's MIL and the European Commission's DigComp. As a result of exploratory factor analysis, seven factors were extracted. Through structural equation modeling (SEM), causal relationships between these factors were identified, revealing the existence of two segments: the social science aspect related to media literacy and the digital skill aspect related to digital competency. From the causal relationships, the instructional hypotheses were formed that set three learning tasks: 1. The Impact of Information and Laws & Rules, 2. Multifaceted and Critical Evaluation of Information, and 3. Digital Skills. This hypothesis would likely result in a curriculum that learners find units meaningfully connected.

articleTitle: Usability Survey of Calligraphy Using Haptic Sense in Virtual Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In today's society, characterized by an aging population and a declining birthrate, there is a need for early detection, prevention, and improvement of frailty in both physical and mental functions. The condition occupies a middle ground between 'healthy states' and ‘states requiring nursing care.’ To address this, we have developed a virtual calligraphy system using haptic sense as one of our support systems. The system uses haptic devices to provide users with feelings similar to those of actual calligraphy, and it can measure the deviations of lines from models and the pressure of strokes for the early detection, prevention, and improvement of frailty. This paper presents an analysis of the results from a usability study of the system, focusing on end-users aged 40 years or older.

articleTitle: Using LLM Artificial Intelligence Systems as Complex SQL Programming Assistants
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Learning database programming such as SQL programming is a challenging task when the queries become more complex. SQL is a declarative language based on relational calculus which describes the definition of the query results instead of describing the procedure or steps used to obtain the query result. Tutorial sessions using tutorial assistances are generally required to support the learning of advanced part of the language. Recently generative AI systems demonstrated question answering capabilities including programming codes generation. This paper verifies the SQL code generating capabilities of four generative AI systems: Bing, Bard, ChatGPT, and Copilot and their suitability as SQL programming assistants.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Code.org's Block-Based Coding Curriculum on Student Motivation in K-12 Education
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In an era where technological skills are essential, integrating coding curriculum within Macao's primary education is becoming increasingly prevalent. However, fostering programming skills among young learners is challenging, particularly when low motivation impedes learning. Code.org, a block-based programming website, has recently seen increasing use in universities, high schools, and primary schools. It incorporates gamification elements, allowing students to learn programming through a game-based challenge. This study employed a quasi-experimental approach to explore the impact of Code.org on enhancing students' motivation to learn coding. The participants comprised 20 grade three students who received three weeks of instruction, with six lessons each week, each lasting 40 minutes. The effectiveness of the Code.org intervention was assessed using the Instructional Materials Motivation Survey (IMMS), which measures the dimensions of the ARCS motivation model: Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. The findings revealed a significant boost in learning motivation across all ARCS dimensions following the Code.org course. The study also demonstrated a strong correlation between these dimensions within the block-based coding curriculum provided by Code.org, suggesting the value of such platforms in motivating and improving programming education in primary schools.

articleTitle: The Effect of K - Means Clustering on Collaborative Filtering in Book Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: As recorded on the Goodreads dataset, around 2 million books exist up until 2017. A recommendation system provides book recommendations based on user profiles. Collaborative Filtering (CF) is one of the methods of recommendation systems. There are several approaches, some of them are neighborhood-based, such as user-based CF and item-based CF. However, the computation is time-consuming, so clustering can be employed beforehand to create a faster model. The clustering will split users into several clusters and use CF to compute rating predictions. The results show that K-Means clustering reduces the inference time in both CF methods. Item-based CF is also found to be better suited to K-Means clustering than user-based CF.

articleTitle: Distinguishing between AI Image Creation and Human Image Creation: Creators vs. Non-creators
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: As artworks created by artificial intelligence (AI) become more and more closely resemble those human-created ones because of the fast development in AI, numerous issues and challenges have emerged. This study explored the difference between creators and non-creators in distinguishing between AI image creation (AIIC) and human image creation (HIC). A total of 22 creators and 28 non-creators participated in this study, and they were asked to identify whether works are AIIC and HIC. The researchers of this study selected 12 AIIC works and 12 HIC works, which are further divided into the following four categories: (I) abstract images, (II) art images, (III) landscape images, and (IV) anime images. The study results showed that (1) humans can intuitively determine whether a work is by AI or by humans (p = 0.000), even when the 24 works were mixed and arranged in a random order on purpose. Nevertheless, the difference was only 13.4%, which means that AI in the near future may replace or even surpass works by humans, making AIIC and HIC no longer distinguishable. (2) When works differed hugely in their style, the study subjects' ability to distinguish between AIIC or HIC decreased substantially. (3) No difference was found between creators and non-creators in their ability to distinguish between AIIC and HIC. (4) No difference was found between male and female subjects in their ability to distinguish between AIIC and HIC. AI graphics has advanced greatly in recent years, allowing people to rapidly create very real-looking images by typing in some simple key words. However, an important question that arises is that whether creators should openly embrace AI or should creators remain as the main force of creation by treating AI as nothing but a tool. Another issue is whether creators should be alarmed by the possible threats or negative effects of AI. While these questions and issues are waiting to be addressed in the future, the emergence of AI is like an opened Pandora's box that forces people to confront new challenges and to advance fast.

articleTitle: Incorporating ChatGPT in English Classrooms: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study reports on the integration of ChatGPT, a cutting-edge AI tool, into English classrooms to enhance students' presentation skills. During a four-month semester, students employed ChatGPT for refining their presentation scripts, searching presentation resources, and improving presentation techniques. The effectiveness of this approach was assessed through pre- and post-project surveys, along with evaluations of student presentations by teachers. Results indicate significant improvements in students' presentation skills in English and in their comprehension of topics. Additionally, teachers reported a reduction in the workload associated with script checking and revision. Despite the current skepticism regarding the use of AI tools like ChatGPT in educational contexts, largely due to a lack of empirical data at the forefront of education technology, this project illustrates potential benefits, particularly in language learning environments. It offers valuable insights and can serve as a foundational reference for the broader educational community in considering the adoption of AI tools.

articleTitle: Applying Integrated Education Platform Technologies for Food and Agriculture Education in Elementary Schools
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: E-Oriented Development (EOD) is considered a solution to inefficient resource utilization in education for old town district regeneration. This study applied integrated education platform technologies for the EOD strategic plan for Zhongxiao Elementary School reconstruction. focused on integrating food and agriculture education with an e-learning technology, aimed at fostering community engagement, sustainability, and leveraging the EOD framework. The study provided practical learning experiences and developed a platform framework to enhance the efforts of food and agriculture education programs by promoting school-community interaction.

articleTitle: FRACTAL Methodology for Industry 4.0 & Society 5.0-Driven New Product Development: Empowering Engineering Students for Startup Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Industry 4.0 brings a new era in design and manufacturing, characterized by the integration of cyber-physical systems (CPS), Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics among other technologies. Society 5.0 aims at using these tools for the wellbeing of humankind. This paradigm shift needs a structured methodology for new product development and management, particularly pertinent for engineering students aspiring to pioneer startups. This work proposes a methodological framework tailored for Society 5.0, providing a strategic approach for engineering students that are willing to create “smart products”. By juxtaposing these technological developments with established human-centered product design principles, this framework equips students with the tools and best practices to harness innovation and drive entrepreneurial success.

articleTitle: A Revising Support Method for Lecture Slides Based on Topic Explanation Quantity and Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In the era of expanding online lectures, the reliance on slides has surged. However, instructors face challenges in creating cohesive slides that align with the broader lecture structure. The process is often burdensome, complicated by the difficulty of objectively evaluating and enhancing one's own slides. To address this, our study introduces a system that assesses lecture slides using a conceptual model derived from a textbook. This system then provides targeted suggestions for edits. By incorporating these proposed edits, instructors can seamlessly refine and improve their slides, offering a practical solution to the challenges associated with slide creation and enhancement.

articleTitle: Effects of Input Enhancement on Vocabulary Learning in Web-based Learning Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Despite the recognition received by technology-enhanced language learning (TELL) in the past decade, the effectiveness of some pedagogical approaches can be as unclear in TELL environments as they are in the traditional in-person classroom. The effects of input enhancement-a type of form-focused instruction-is one such case. This study investigates the effects of input enhancement in a web-based vocabulary learning environment. There are two types of input enhancement: input with an extra-recall (Type I) and text enhancement with increased font size in context (Type II). The participants were 34 first-year university students who used a prototype system for web-based vocabulary learning and received posttests immediately. Three pedagogical approaches were integrated into the system: baseline learning without input enhancement, vocabulary learning with Type I enhancement, and vocabulary learning with Type II enhancement. The results of the immediate posttests showed that the learning approach with Type II enhancement tends to outperform the other approaches in the web-based vocabulary learning environment.

articleTitle: Perceiving Web-based Language Learning and Collaborative Online International Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The use of technology in Japanese language learning has been increasing after the COVID-19 pandemic. This paper discusses the learners' perceptions of learning Japanese using technology, particularly through web-based applications (B-apps) and Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL). The research was conducted among first-semester students majoring in Japanese literature at B University. The research method in this study is a mixed method, which combines quantitative data analysis obtained from questionnaires and qualitative data analysis obtained from focus group discussions. The research findings indicate that learning with B-apps will be more effective if other aspects of language learning such as orthography and contextual use of the language require reshaping and restructuring to achieve impactful learning. While learning with COIL is better conducted after the first semester so that the learners already have a sufficient foundation in Japanese to communicate confidently.

articleTitle: Development of a Technological Tool to Improve the Learning of Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In traditional education, working with children with autism spectrum disorder represents a significant challenge for educators. However, the use of technology has provided new opportunities that offer more resources adapted to people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This work aims to present the development of a technological tool based on a program developed in Python language, which offers nine different types of activities that aim to develop cognitive skills in students with ASD. Also, the development of a keyboard that facilitates the student's interaction with the program is presented. It is suggested that this tool can improve multisensory and cognitive development in students with ASD.

articleTitle: Experiential Media Wall Utilizing Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This research suggests implementing an interactive experiential media wall incorporating hand gesture recognition technology to improve the educational experience in media wall exhibition environments and executing usability survey and analyses. The proposed media wall allows users to explore contents through hand gestures on a map-based interface, providing information about heritage sites based on actual location data. We develop the overall system using the Unity 3D engine to recognize and interact with the hand gesture when the user stays in the correct hand gesture posture for a certain period. As a result, it was confirmed that the proposed approach exhibited high usability overall, regardless of gender and age. Additionally, using hand gestures for media wall interaction was key in increasing satisfaction with the educational experience.

articleTitle: Edu MEAL: Food Education Application That Promotes Taste Education
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This paper presents an application, “Edu MEAL”, that aims to facilitate taste education for children and enable them to engage in taste education regularly. Edu MEAL is designed for children who interact with the application after meals to record their impressions of the food they ate. The application uses a sentence-generating AI to provide examples of meal impressions based on the menus, which can help children pay attention to the taste of the food and enhance their vocabulary and expression skills. We conducted a user study with an 8-year-old boy who used Edu MEAL and we reported on the effects of the application on the user the system's interface, and the usage experience.

articleTitle: Research on Support System for Programmatic Thinking Based on Metacognition of Instructional Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In Japan, programming education has been mandated in elementary, junior high, and high school curricula since the publication of the Courses of Study in 2020. In particular, elementary school programming education prioritizes the development of logical thinking skills, focusing on programming thinking, such as problem identification and action decomposition, rather than mere coding proficiency. This study aims to design a training system that enhances logical thinking skills through instructional dialogues. In the proposed system, users provide instructions to a virtual robot via dialogues, and the robot executes actions accordingly. Subsequently, users can review the robot's movements in the virtual space. Essentially, the proposed system offers metacognition, which serves as objective feedback, enabling users to enhance their logical thinking abilities. To assess the effectiveness of our system, we conducted two tests: pretests and posttests following the use of the system, and the results confirmed its efficacy.

articleTitle: The Effects of Gamification and VR in Encouraging Pro-Environmental Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Emerging gamification and immersive technology encourage individuals, especially teenagers, to engage in a behavior, such as online shopping behavior, learning behavior, prosocial behavior, etc. Many current studies showed that the use of gamification and immersive technology would positively predict individuals' intention towards a behavior. The present study aims to examine the impact of gamification and VR in promoting low-carbon actions and pro-environmental habits. Using VR cave with gamified elements, the results showed that enjoyment and environmental responsibility significantly predict low-carbon action of individuals, whereas social gain has no significant impact on low-carbon intention. Practical contributions are discussed.

articleTitle: Predicting the Risk of Course Change in Online Education Using the Causal Shapley Method
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The proliferation of online education has generated new demands for improving the quality of education through an understanding of student behavior patterns. This study introduces an approach to elucidate the complex relationship between student behavior and educational outcomes, specifically focusing on predicting course changes in online schools. To enhance the interpretability of the predictive model, we introduced the Causal Shapley value, which incorporates causal inference, in comparison to traditional SHAP values, to assess the impact of features. This approach confirmed that attendance rate and the number of students per campus are significant features for predicting course changes. The Causal Shapley value provided new insights, especially highlighting the number of students per campus as a causal factor in dropout predictions, offering a finer perspective on the impact of features than traditional SHAP values. This methodology goes beyond mere correlations, allowing for a deeper understanding of how features influence prediction outcomes, thereby providing vital information for educational institutions to design intervention strategies tailored to the individual needs of students.

articleTitle: Application of SPOCs-Based Blended Teaching into Explicit Instruction on Syntactically Complex Constituents
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study constructs SPOCs-based blended instruction with explicit attention to syntactic complexity and investigates, through an exploratory study, the effects of such instruction on EFL learners' syntactic awareness. With grammatical error correction and syntactic word-order tasks conducted before and after a training program, the results reveal a significant improvement in learners' syntactic awareness of syntactic patterns in fiction and academic writing. The results suggest that the SPOCs-based training program with a register focus on syntactic complexity benefits EFL learners' metalinguistic awareness, especially in academic discourse. The present study sheds light on the classroom-oriented research to construct SPOCs-based blended teaching approaches and evaluate the effectiveness of such pedagogy.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithm, Scaling Technique and the Accuracy: An Application to Educational Data
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) applications in educational data mining have become an increasingly popular research area. Literature indicates a lack of research investigating the impact of data scaling techniques, ML algorithms, and the nature of data on the classification's accuracy. This study aims to fulfill the above. In that direction, we use three linear and three non-linear ML classifiers and six scaling techniques to evaluate the impact of the data scaling technique and the ML algorithm on four selected educational datasets. According to the experimental outcomes for data set #1, classification accuracy was significantly influenced (p-value < 0.01) by the nature of the data. All the performance indicators except detection rate and prevalence were highly influenced by the type of ML technique used for the classification. Furthermore, there was a significant (p-value < 0.05) interaction impact of two-way interactions of the nature of the data and the type of ML technique for F1 value and balanced accuracy. Further analysis indicates that the classification accuracy varies with the level of the class variable.

articleTitle: The Impact of AI Tools in Education Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly gaining popularity and influence in our society. New emerging artificial intelligence tools (AIT) are released to the public and are gaining momentum with a growing debate about the possible negative and positive effects of these new tools on students' skills, specifically their emotional intelligence (EI). This article addresses the scarcity of research related to Artificial Intelligence Tools AIT specifically ChatGPT, its possible negative effect on the EI of engineering and non-engineering students, and their level of EI. We built an online questionnaire that we shared electronically with students worldwide on the Facebook platform and in classrooms by uni-versity professors. We used Wong and Law's WLEIS self-report emotional intelligence scale and adapted it for our research. Most answers received are from Tunisia and Hungary. The findings demonstrate that students who study engineering tend to have lower emotional intelligence (EI) than non-engineering students. Additionally, the use of ChatGPT appears to have a somewhat detrimental impact on students' EI abilities, regardless of whether or not they have any concerns regarding artificial intelligence technology (AIT). However, it should be noted that students are still utilizing ChatGPT for both personal and academic purposes

articleTitle: Development of 360-Degree Virtual Reality Chinese CLIL Learning Material for Intercultural Understanding Integrated with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for Regional Revitalization
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study presents the development of 360-degree VR Chinese language learning materials, integrating intercultural understanding with SDGs to revitalize regional heritage. The material uses VR and CLIL methodologies to transcend physical boundaries, offering immersive, narrative-driven experiences in Lugang, Taiwan. By simulating realistic scenarios, it aims to enhance language proficiency and subject comprehension. This innovative approach could redefine foreign language education, fostering global competence and contributing to the sustainability of local cultures. The research underscores the potential for using VR in higher education to address contemporary educational challenges.

articleTitle: Crochet-Together: Cultivating Positive Emotional Well-being with the Touch of Technology-Enhanced Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Emotional well-being is a growing concern in Malaysia, and this study aims to address it by proposing the mobile application ‘Crochet-Together’ as a tool to promote positive emotional well-being among young adults. By leveraging the therapeutic benefits of crocheting and the Technology-Enhanced Learning, Crochet-Together serves as a platform to cultivate the hobby while nurturing emotional well-being. An online survey was conducted prior to the application's development to explore the impact of crocheting on young adults' well-being and gather user requirements. Upon development, a separate survey was done to assess users' perceived effectiveness in addressing emotional well-being and to evaluate the application's usability using the System Usability Scale. The findings suggest that engaging in crocheting has a positive impact on young adults, enhancing their mood, reducing stress, and promoting relaxation. Besides that, the study also highlights the potential of the Technology-Enhanced Learning to promote emotional well-being. The high SUS score (89) obtained underlines the favorable usability evaluation of Crochet-Together. By utilizing the insights gained, future enhancements in terms of the functionality of the tool can be made to further support these users' needs and enhance their crocheting skills and experiences amongst young crocheters.

articleTitle: AMPNet: Academic Multi-Task Prediction Network for Students' Grade and Graduation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Machine learning based academic performance prediction of students is showing great significance in ensuring the good quality of higher education. However, most methods only focus on predicting academic performance in a single aspect (such as only grade) or for students in a single Major. To address this issue, this paper designs an academic multi-task prediction network model called AMPNet for both grade prediction and graduation prediction of all majors in universities. It consists of three parts: the LSTM part, attention part, and feature fusion part. The LSTM part extracts the time series features of students' historical terms and predicts the grade points of the next term. Then these features are further refined by the terms and attributes attention part. Finally, the refined features are input into the feature fusion part, concatenating the input major delay-graduation embedding, and outputs the prediction results of both grade and graduation status. Comparative experiments show that the proposed AMPNet model provides good performance in grade point prediction, and it significantly outperforms mainstream machine learning prediction models in graduation prediction, and ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of three key modules: major delay-graduation embedding, terms attention, and attributes attention.

articleTitle: On Combining the Potential of Social Robots and ChatGPT for Enhanced Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This systematic literature review examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI), specifically that of social robots and ChatGPT, on education. This study thoroughly assesses the diverse applications of AI in pedagogy. It emphasizes the potential synergy between social robots and ChatGPT and their transformative impact on teaching, learning, and academic outcomes. By comprehensively examining various scholarly publications, this review highlights the significant influence of social robots in facilitating emotional involvement, collaborative learning, and immersive educational situations. Additionally, it clarifies the mechanism by which ChatGPT enables personalized instruction, immediate knowledge sharing, and academic assistance. Furthermore, it highlights the difficulties and ethical complexities of incorporating AI technology in education. This necessitates the development of a careful and deliberate strategy to ensure data privacy, reduce excessive reliance on AI, and maintain the indispensable role of human educators. This review comprehensively analyzes existing research to understand the evolution of AI-driven education. It discusses the significant contributions of social robots and ChatGPT in shaping an educational landscape that prioritizes effective pedagogical methods, fosters inclusive learning environments, and achieves a balance between technological advancements and human interaction

articleTitle: Decoding Academic Language: The Symbiotic Relationship Between Boosters, Hedges, and Voice in EAP
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This research represents a pioneering endeavor to delineate the intricate relationship between linguistic boosters and hedges in varying voice constructs within the domain of English for Academic Purposes (EAP). Drawing upon a comprehensive corpus of academic English, we systematically investigated the nuanced ways in which these rhetorical devices are deployed across different academic disciplines and authorial backgrounds. A key innovation of our study lies in its novel exploration of how boosters and hedges are utilized distinctly in active and passive voice contexts, a facet of academic language that has been previously overlooked. Our findings reveal significant patterns of usage, highlighting both commonalities and disparities in the application of these linguistic features. The study substantiates the hypothesis that the employment of hedges and boosters is not uniform, but rather subject to variations influenced by voice structures. Moreover, the research underscores the impact of author identity and academic experience on the utilization of these rhetorical elements, contributing valuable insights to the ongoing discourse in academic linguistics. The practical ramifications of this study extend to EAP teaching methodologies, indicating avenues for refining linguistic instruction. In addition, the research lays a foundational basis for future scholarly inquiry into the complex dynamics of language use in academic settings.

articleTitle: Measuring Student Satisfaction Based on Analysis of Physical Parameters in Smart Classroom
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Several factors related to the physical environment, including temperature, environmental noise, CO2 levels, air pressure, humidity, and the lecturer's vocal delivery, significantly impact student satisfaction. Evaluating, quantifying, and enhancing these factors can significantly contribute to enhancing students' satisfaction with lecture quality. The objective of this study is to assess students' satisfaction regarding the quality of lectures through an analysis of data obtained from a variety of smart devices that record physical environmental parameters. In this study, the machine learning techniques employed encompass Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), K-nearest neighbors (KNN), and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). Additionally, the deep learning models utilized comprise Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM). The findings of this study suggest that, on the whole, deep learning models demonstrate superior performance when it comes to classifying data about this particular problem, as compared to traditional machine learning models. Notably, the CNN model emerges as the top performer among all the models assessed, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 74.62%. it is worth mentioning that the decision tree exhibits the highest accuracy among classical machine learning models.

articleTitle: Graph Attention-Enhanced Knowledge Tracing: Unveiling Exercise Variability and Long-Term Dependencies
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) is vital for predicting students' mastery of knowledge concepts (KCs) based on interactive data from their practice sessions, facilitating adaptive learning resource recommendations. Despite the effectiveness of existing models, challenges persist, such as handling long-term dependencies in RNN-based models and real-time tracing of knowledge states across various KCs in attention mechanism-based models. Additionally, latent information within exercises and variations in difficulty levels among exercises under the same KC are often overlooked. To address these challenges, we propose a Graph Attention Mechanism-based Knowledge Tracing model (GAKT). Our approach involves constructing a bipartite graph to represent the exercise-KC relationship, integrating a difficulty vector into the interaction vectors of exercises, and utilizing Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to extract embeddings. Incorporating an attention mechanism, our model features a knowledge state revival module that captures long-term dependencies and provides real-time tracing of students' knowledge states. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GAKT outperforms the state-of-the-art graph-based KT model (GIKT) by an average of 2.3% in terms of AUC across three datasets, showing the importance of high-order information for deeper associations between KCs and exercises in the KT task. This study contributes to advancing knowledge tracing methodologies in the field.

articleTitle: Based on Clustering Label Generation for View Type Noisy Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Based on the previously designed View type detection system, there is already a comprehensive algorithm framework for achieving complete View type detection functionality. Due to the increasing variety and quantity of apps nowadays, as well as the different scenarios contained in each app, we want to collect more data for model training and testing. However, the cost of using manual annotation increases with the number of views that need to be detected. This paper implements a clustering based automatic generation of labels to achieve semi supervised learning. However, considering that the automatically generated labels may contain incorrect labels (which are inconsistent with the manually annotated results), Co-teaching method was adopted to perform noisy learning on the data containing incorrect labels. To reduce the error rate of label generation, we improved the DPC-MND algorithm by introducing a dynamic truncation threshold and improving its allocation strategy, thereby enhancing the algorithm's ability to handle noisy or irrelevant points. And established a mapping method for clustering centers to labels, achieving automated generation of labels.

articleTitle: Excel-Ling in Data Visualization: Evaluating Microsoft Excel's User-Friendliness, Visual Appeal, and Reputation Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study examines how Microsoft Excel's reputation, visual appeal and ease of use affect its use for data visualization tasks. Excel is a popular tool for managing, visualizing and analysing data in many different industries due to its functionality and accessibility. The study focuses on Excel's usability, i.e. its feature-rich user interface, ability to create visually appealing graphics, and overall ease of use. It also examines how users perceive Excel's reliability and trustworthiness and the important role Excel's reputation plays in user preference and loyalty. Based on a structured survey of students who have experience with data analysis, the study concludes that Excel is the better choice for data visualization due to its intuitive design and ability to create attractive and informative graphics. The study highlights Excel's good reputation, which not only shapes user behaviour, but also ensures good word of mouth that expands the platform's user base. According to the study, Excel's reputation, ease of use and visual capabilities are related and have a significant impact on how often it is used for data visualization. The study suggests integrating Excel into academic curricula, emphasizing the pedagogical benefits of Excel, and recommending future research to investigate the impact of Excel in different educational and professional contexts.

articleTitle: Coaching in Hybrid Workplace: An Examination of Face-to-Face and Online Coaching to Enhance Self-Efficacy and Knowledge Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study, grounded in Bandura's social cognitive theory, investigates the effects of coaching on knowledge creation and the mediating effect of self-efficacy. Utilizing data from a 3-wave longitudinal field study involving 290 employees within a top 100 chain enterprise in China, analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The findings reveal that face-to-face facilitation positively influences all four dimensions of knowledge creation, while face-to-face guidance has a diminishing effect on most dimensions. Interestingly, online guidance demonstrates a positive impact on the combination and internationalization while online facilitation did not affect any SECI process. Furthermore, the study identified that self-efficacy at work serves as a mediator in the relationship between face-to-face facilitation and knowledge creation. Theoretical and practical implications are discussed.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Enhancing Physical Education: A systematic literature review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: This study aims to systematically review the application of Artificial intelligence (AI) technology to enhance physical education (PE). To this end, 104 journals in the databases of Baidu Scholar, Google Scholar, and King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang Library from 2014 to October 2023 were selected as research objects, and the research results were analyzed using the content analysis method. The analysis results show that the first research on this topic was conducted in 2014, and the Number of relevant studies has increased yearly, especially during the pandemic. In addition, these studies were mainly conducted in a combination of quantitative and qualitative, mainly journal articles. In addition, the samples of these studies are from each academic section, and most of the studies are conducted by college students. The analysis focuses on article distribution, publication time, research content, technology selection, and current and future challenges and summarizes the development trend, specific applications, benefits, and challenges of AI sports. The findings of the studies revealed that AI technology in PE can improve students' physical achievement, cognition, and learning habits. On the other hand, AI technology can enhance the effect of PE so that students have a greater interest in learning sports. Finally, some suggestions for future research are put forward.

articleTitle: Evaluation Framework of Collaborative Competence in Project-based Collaborative Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Collaborative competence plays a crucial role in individual learning, team collaboration and social development. However, the evaluation of collaborative competence often overlooks the real collaborative situation and lacks behavioral analysis of the collaborative process. To address this gap, this study specifically focuses on evaluating collaborative competence in project-based collaborative learning adopting a procedural behavior perspective, an evaluation framework for collaborative competence in project-based learning was developed. This framework consists of four categories (negotiated interaction, supportive interaction, management monitoring, and emotional regulation), further divided into 15 subcategories. The weights of each indicator were determined using the Analytic Hierarchy Process. The results indicate that “Negotiated interaction” and “Management monitoring” account for a relatively high proportion among the four categories. Among the subcategories, “Express viewpoints”, “Coordinate resources or actions”, “Evaluate others' viewpoints”, and “Provide support” were found to be significant. Moreover, the effectiveness of this evaluation framework was verified in real project-based collaborative learning environment, offering valuable insights for analyzing the collaborative learning process and providing learning interventions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Solution Results of Code Writing Problems for Basic Object-Oriented Programming Study in University Java Programming Course
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: To support novice students in learning Java programming, we have implemented the web-based Java Programming Learning Assistant System (JPLAS). In JPLAS, one of the implemented exercise problems is the Code Writing Problem (CWP), where students are tasked with crafting a source code capable of passing provided test cases. The accuracy of the answer code is verified by executing it on JUnit. Previously, we generated seven CWP instances accompanying with test codes, focusing on six fundamental Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts. These assignments were intended for use in a Java programming course at Okayama University, where OOP is a crucial topic. Despite their relevance, these assignments were not assigned to students for completion. In this paper, we present an analysis of the solution results obtained from the CWP instances. Our findings indicate that the students demonstrated a comprehensive understanding of basic OOP concepts, as the majority of them successfully solved all the generated instances and achieved a 100% correct rate. Only three students did not complete all the instances. Based on these results, we conclude that the proposed approach is valid and effective in facilitating student learning of OOP concepts.

articleTitle: Designing an Application for Track the Disease Transmission on Hospital Workers by Safety Climate Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Disease transmission in a hospital has become a crucial problem nowadays. Especially when the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) happened, many hospital workers were infected by this virus. The disease can be transmitted through hospital workers, patients, and other health care facilities. However, hospital workers have the most impact on disease transmission because they have direct contact with patients or move from one room to another room frequently. Based on the interview that was done by the author to one of the hospitals in Bandung, Indonesia showed that there was an increase in coronavirus cases from 2020 to 2021 caused by non-compliance of hospital workers in implementing the standard precautions. The awareness of hospital workers to the standard precautions is needed to decrease the disease transmission cases in hospitals. Therefore, this research will design an application that can track hospital workers' safety with a safety climate approach to ensure that every hospital worker is in safe and healthy condition while working. The outcome of the design thinking methodology is 11 need statements, which are used as a guide for designing application interfaces. Conversely, the application's questionnaire function will be employed using the safety climate strategy. Three hypotheses are approved and two are discarded as a result of hypothesis testing. using 26 indicators in all. Later on, the application's questionnaire questions will incorporate these 26 indications.

articleTitle: Impressing Museum Visitors by Having Them Answer Questions Toward the Realization of an Interactive Viewing Support System
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Education Technology (ICIET)
abstract: In this study, we examine how museum visitor's experience can be enhanced and made memorable long after their visit by engaging them in interactive question-and-answer sessions about the exhibits. Our hypothesis is that a viewing system in which museum exhibits pose questions to visitors and they respond based on their own interpretations will enable even those accustomed to viewing exhibits to have a more memorable experience. In the experiment, eight subjects viewed exhibits at the National Museum of Ethnology (Minpaku). As part of our process, they answered questions related to the exhibits. Two days later, we conducted follow-up interviews. Experimental results indicate that questions prompting participants to imagine scenarios from their daily lives are more likely to leave lasting impression. Therefore, an interactive question-and-answer approach to viewing exhibits appears to be effective in creating a more memorable museum experience.
